items.question: What performance credit may be taken for engines delivering above-specification power (a positive power margin)?
options: No performance credit is to be taken for above specification power
Full performance credit may be taken
50% of the power margin may be credited
Credit is limited to takeoff only, not landing
items.explanation: The performance charts are predicated on engines that deliver specification power; no performance credit is to be taken for above-specification power (positive power margin).
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: GENERAL / ENGINE HEALTH (p.4-1)

items.question: Per WIND ACCOUNTABILITY, unless otherwise authorized by operating regulations, what performance credit/penalty applies to headwind and tailwind components?
options: No more than 50% credit for the headwind performance increase, and 150% penalty applied to the tailwind performance decrement
Full 100% credit for headwind, and no penalty for tailwind
No credit for headwind, and no penalty for tailwind
50% credit for both headwind and tailwind equally
items.explanation: The pilot is not authorized to credit more than 50 percent of the performance increase from an actual headwind, and must reduce performance by 150 percent of the decrement resulting from an actual tailwind component.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: WIND ACCOUNTABILITY (p.4-1)

items.question: For the Category A horizontal takeoff procedure, in what range and increments is the Takeoff Decision Point (TDP) airspeed selectable, and how is Vtoss defined?
options: Selectable in 1-knot increments between 30 and 48 knots; Vtoss = TDP + 15 knots
Selectable in 5-knot increments between 20 and 40 knots; Vtoss = TDP + 10 knots
Selectable in 1-knot increments between 35 and 55 knots; Vtoss = TDP + 20 knots
Fixed at 40 knots; Vtoss = TDP + 15 knots
items.explanation: TDP is selectable in 1-knot increments between 30 and 48 knots, with Vtoss defined as TDP + 15 knots, permitting payload to be traded against available field length.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: CATEGORY A HORIZONTAL TAKEOFF DISTANCE (p.4-1)

items.question: What two operational questions does the S-92 Category A variable-TDP takeoff procedure allow a pilot to answer?
options: Determine the maximum takeoff gross weight for an available field length, or determine the required field length for a desired takeoff gross weight
Determine only the maximum passenger count for a given fuel load
Determine only the required crosswind limit for a given TDP
Determine the noise certification stage applicable to the flight
items.explanation: The variable-TDP Category A procedure lets a pilot trade payload against available field length: given a field length, determine the maximum takeoff gross weight; or given a desired takeoff gross weight, determine the required field length.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: CATEGORY A HORIZONTAL TAKEOFF DISTANCE (p.4-1)

items.question: How does a lower TDP speed affect Category A rejected/continued takeoff field length and maximum takeoff gross weight?
options: A lower TDP speed gives shorter RTO/CTO field lengths but also a lower maximum takeoff gross weight
A lower TDP speed gives longer field lengths and a higher maximum takeoff gross weight
TDP speed has no effect on either field length or maximum gross weight
A lower TDP speed only affects landing distance, not takeoff distance
items.explanation: RTO and CTO distances, and maximum takeoff/landing gross weight, are both directly proportional to TDP speed: lower TDP speeds mean shorter field lengths but also lower maximum gross weights, and vice versa.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: CATEGORY A HORIZONTAL TAKEOFF DISTANCE (p.4-1)

items.question: For a Category A ground level helipad takeoff, what does the "maximum reject TDP" represent?
options: The highest height from which a rejected landing can be accomplished without damage to the aircraft
The lowest height from which the fly away maneuver can be accomplished with 15 feet of clearance
The minimum required field length for any takeoff
The maximum permitted obstacle height near the helipad
items.explanation: The maximum reject TDP is the highest height from which a rejected landing can be accomplished without damage to the aircraft, as distinct from the minimum fly-away TDP.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: CATEGORY A VERTICAL GROUND LEVEL HELIPAD (p.4-2)

items.question: For a Category A ground level helipad takeoff, what does the "minimum fly-away TDP" represent?
options: The lowest height from which the fly-away maneuver can be accomplished with 15 feet of clearance from the helipad altitude
The highest height from which a rejected landing can be accomplished without damage
The maximum takeoff gross weight permitted at the helipad
The horizontal distance required to reach 35 feet above the helipad
items.explanation: The minimum fly-away TDP is the lowest height from which the fly-away maneuver can be accomplished with 15 feet of clearance from the helipad altitude.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: CATEGORY A VERTICAL GROUND LEVEL HELIPAD (p.4-2)

items.question: What safety concern arises if the minimum fly-away TDP is greater than the maximum reject TDP for a given weight/altitude/temperature?
options: Safe continued flight or landing is not assured if an engine fails while climbing between the two TDPs
There is no concern; the aircraft can always land safely between the TDPs
It only affects fuel planning, not safety
It simply means the helipad is undersized for Category A operations
items.explanation: If the minimum fly-away TDP exceeds the maximum reject TDP, safe continued flight or landing is not assured for an engine failure occurring while climbing between the two TDPs.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: CATEGORY A VERTICAL GROUND LEVEL HELIPAD (p.4-2)

items.question: How is the Category A ground level helipad "take off field length" defined?
options: The horizontal distance from the helipad required to reach 35 feet above the helipad or obstacle altitude at a Vtoss climb with 2 minute power selected, after an engine failure at the minimum TDP
The total distance needed for a rolling takeoff regardless of engine status
The distance from TDP to attaining Vy only
The distance required to descend from cruise altitude to the helipad
items.explanation: Take off field length is the horizontal distance, measured from the helipad, required to reach 35 feet above the helipad or obstacle altitude at a Vtoss climb with 2 minute power selected, following an engine failure at the minimum TDP.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: CATEGORY A VERTICAL GROUND LEVEL HELIPAD (p.4-2)

items.question: How is the Category A ground level helipad "balked landing distance" defined?
options: The horizontal distance from the helipad required to reach 45 feet above the helipad, or 35 feet above the obstacle (whichever is higher), at a Vtoss climb after an engine failure at the LDP
The distance required to stop the aircraft during a rejected landing
The distance from the LDP to touchdown during a normal landing
The distance flown during a go-around at Vy
items.explanation: Balked landing distance is the horizontal distance from the helipad required to reach 45 feet above the helipad or 35 feet above the obstacle, whichever is higher, at a Vtoss climb following an engine failure at the LDP.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: CATEGORY A VERTICAL GROUND LEVEL HELIPAD (p.4-2)

items.question: If there are no obstacles over 10 feet in the balked landing path, what minimum Landing Decision Point (LDP) may the pilot choose?
options: 125 feet, providing 25 feet of clearance above helipad level (15 feet clearance of a 10 foot obstacle)
55 feet, matching the balked landing climb speed in KIAS
35 feet, matching the takeoff field length obstacle-clearance height
items.explanation: With no obstacles over 10 feet in the balked landing path, the pilot can choose the minimum LDP of 125 feet, providing 25 feet of clearance above helipad level (15 feet of clearance over a 10 foot obstacle).
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: CATEGORY A VERTICAL GROUND LEVEL HELIPAD (p.4-2)

items.question: For a Category A vertical takeoff, if an obstacle is close enough to and low enough over the helipad that it lies within the obstacle exempt region, how must the pilot treat it when determining minimum fly-away TDP?
options: It can be disregarded — no correction to the minimum fly-away TDP is required
It must always be added to the minimum fly-away TDP regardless of its height or distance
It automatically cancels the takeoff regardless of aircraft weight
It must be treated as reducing the maximum reject TDP instead
items.explanation: Obstacles within the defined obstacle exempt region are guaranteed at least 15 feet of clearance along the takeoff profile due to their low height and close proximity to the pad, and are therefore exempt from obstacle clearance consideration when determining minimum fly-away TDP.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: CATEGORY A GROUND LEVEL HELIPAD OBSTACLE EXEMPTION REGION FOR TAKEOFF (p.4-38)

items.question: For a Category A vertical takeoff, if an obstacle lies outside the obstacle exempt region (i.e. it is high enough and/or far enough from the pad), what must the pilot do to the minimum fly-away TDP?
options: Correct it by adding the obstacle height to the no-obstacle minimum fly-away TDP
Ignore the obstacle since only obstacles within the exempt region matter
Reduce gross weight by an amount equal to the obstacle height in feet
Add the obstacle height to the maximum reject TDP instead
items.explanation: If an obstacle falls outside the obstacle exempt region, the minimum fly-away TDP must be corrected by adding the obstacle height to it; if that corrected TDP then exceeds the maximum reject TDP, a Category A takeoff cannot be performed for the planned weight, altitude, temperature and obstacle.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: CATEGORY A GROUND LEVEL HELIPAD OBSTACLE EXEMPTION REGION FOR TAKEOFF (p.4-38)

items.question: Per the notes on the Category A Horizontal Takeoff and Landing Gross Weight chart, what minimum TDP speed applies when the crosswind component exceeds 20 knots?
items.explanation: With a crosswind component greater than 20 knots, the minimum TDP speed for Category A horizontal operations is 45 KIAS, higher than the normal 30 knot minimum TDP baseline.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-9 usage notes (p.4-12)

items.question: What is the fundamental performance guarantee that distinguishes a correctly flown Category A takeoff/landing from a Category B one?
options: Category A, flown within the approved weight/altitude/temperature/field-length/wind conditions, guarantees continued safe flight and landing after an engine failure; Category B does not provide this guarantee
Category A and Category B provide an identical guarantee following an engine failure
Category B guarantees continued flight after an engine failure, while Category A does not
The distinction is only about cabin configuration and has no bearing on engine-failure outcomes
items.explanation: Category A takeoff and landing procedures, flown at the approved weight, altitude, temperature, field length and wind conditions, guarantee continued safe flight and landing after an engine failure. Operating outside those approved conditions, or under Category B, does not carry this guarantee.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec II: TAKEOFF AND LANDING PROCEDURES (p.2-29)

items.question: During Category A takeoff and landing maneuvers, what is the Non-Flying Pilot's (NFP) role with respect to TDP/LDP?
options: Announce when the aircraft attains the TDP or LDP airspeed and/or altitude, and call out deviations from required performance parameters
Take over the flight controls at the TDP so the Flying Pilot can monitor instruments
Remain silent until the aircraft is on the ground to avoid distracting the Flying Pilot
Only handle radio communications during Category A maneuvers
items.explanation: The Non-Flying Pilot supports the Flying Pilot by announcing when the aircraft attains the TDP or LDP airspeed/altitude, and by calling out when actual performance (e.g. Nr range, ground track, or Vtoss) deviates from what is required for the maneuver.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec II: TAKEOFF AND LANDING PROCEDURES (p.2-29)

items.question: What is the maximum crosswind component for Category A horizontal takeoffs and landings?
items.explanation: Category A horizontal takeoffs and landings are limited to 35 knots of crosswind component or less.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: CROSSWIND LIMITS (p.4-1)

items.question: What is the maximum crosswind component for Category A ground level helipad takeoffs and landings?
items.explanation: Category A ground level helipad takeoffs and landings are limited to 22 knots of crosswind component or less.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: CROSSWIND LIMITS (p.4-1)

items.question: In the Category A horizontal takeoff profile (Figure 4-7), what power is used for the horizontal acceleration from the 10 ft hover?
items.explanation: Figure 4-7 shows the horizontal acceleration made at hover Q + 10%, in the normal, rejected and continued takeoff alike.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-7 Cat A Horizontal Takeoff Procedures (p.4-10)

items.question: In the normal (all engines) Category A horizontal takeoff of Figure 4-7, how does the climb continue after the TDP?
options: Level acceleration to Vy at 100% Nr
Climbing acceleration to 80 KIAS at 100% Nr
Climbing acceleration to Vy at 105% Nr
items.explanation: After the TDP in a normal takeoff, Figure 4-7 shows a climbing acceleration to Vy at 105% Nr.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-7 Cat A Horizontal Takeoff Procedures (p.4-10)

items.question: In the Category A horizontal continued takeoff (engine failure after TDP), what speed and rotor speed does Figure 4-7 show for the OEI climb?
options: Vtoss at 100% Nr, gear up with a positive rate of climb
Vy at 105% Nr, gear up at 200 ft
Vtoss at 105% Nr, gear left down
Vy at 100% Nr, gear up at 35 ft
items.explanation: Figure 4-7 shows OEI acceleration to Vtoss, then the OEI climb at Vtoss and 100% Nr, with the gear raised once a positive rate of climb is established.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-7 Cat A Horizontal Takeoff Procedures (p.4-10)

items.question: At what height does the Category A horizontal continued takeoff distance end in Figure 4-7?
items.explanation: The continued takeoff distance in Figure 4-7 is measured from the 10 ft hover to the point where the aircraft reaches 35 ft.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-7 Cat A Horizontal Takeoff Procedures (p.4-10)

items.question: With a crosswind component greater than 20 knots, what correction applies to the Figure 4-8 Category A horizontal rejected and continued takeoff distance?
items.explanation: A note on Figure 4-8 says to add 500 ft to the chart distance when the crosswind component exceeds 20 knots (and the minimum TDP speed becomes 45 KIAS).
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-8 Cat A Horizontal Rejected and Continued Takeoff Distances (p.4-11)

items.question: On Figure 4-9 the Vtoss scale is labelled 45 (30) up to 60 (45). What does the number in brackets show?
options: The OEI rate of climb in 100 fpm
items.explanation: The Figure 4-9 scale is headed 'VTOSS (TDP) ~ KTS': each Vtoss is paired with its TDP, since Vtoss = TDP + 15 knots.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-9 Cat A Horizontal Takeoff and Landing Gross Weight (p.4-12)

items.question: Figure 4-12 (OEI forward climb at takeoff safety speed) is drawn for which configuration?
options: 2 minute power, Vtoss, 100% Nr, gear down
Maximum continuous power, Vy, 100% Nr, gear up
30 second power, Vtoss, 105% Nr, gear down
2 minute power, Vy, 105% Nr, gear up
items.explanation: Figure 4-12 is headed single engine, 2 minute power, takeoff safety speed, 100% Nr, gear down.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-12 OEI Forward Climb Performance, Takeoff Safety Speed (p.4-22)

items.question: Figure 4-13 (OEI forward climb at best rate of climb speed) is drawn for which configuration?
options: Maximum continuous power, 100% Nr, gear up
Maximum continuous power, 105% Nr, gear down
items.explanation: Figure 4-13 is headed single CT7-8A engine, maximum continuous power, best rate of climb speed, 100% Nr, gear up.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-13 OEI Forward Climb Performance, Best Rate of Climb Speed (p.4-23)

items.question: In the Figure 4-13 OEI climb, how much must the rate of climb be reduced at 26,000 lb with RIPS on (manual HEAVY mode) and anti-ice on?
items.explanation: The Figure 4-13 table gives a 440 fpm reduction for RIPS on (manual HEAVY) with anti-ice on at 26,000 lb, against 85 for anti-ice alone and 35 for landing gear down.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-13 OEI Forward Climb Performance, Best Rate of Climb Speed (p.4-23)

items.question: In the Figure 4-12 OEI climb at Vtoss, what rate-of-climb reduction applies for the air conditioner on at 16,000 lb?
items.explanation: The Figure 4-12 table gives 105 fpm for air conditioner on at 16,000 lb (100 fpm for anti-ice on).
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-12 OEI Forward Climb Performance, Takeoff Safety Speed (p.4-22)

items.question: Where is the Landing Decision Point in the Category A horizontal landing profile (Figure 4-14)?
items.explanation: Figure 4-14 shows a descent at 600 fpm and 50 KIAS to the decision point at 50 KIAS and 200 ft AGL.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-14 Cat A Horizontal Landing Profile (p.4-24)

items.question: In the Category A horizontal balked landing (Figure 4-14), what speed is flown in the climb-out?
options: Vtoss at 105% Nr, then accelerate to Vy
70 KIAS at 100% Nr, then accelerate to BROC speed
55 KIAS at 100% Nr, then accelerate to 80 KIAS
50 KIAS at 100% Nr, then accelerate to Vtoss
items.explanation: Figure 4-14 shows acceleration to 70 KIAS with 35 ft minimum clearance, a climb at 70 KIAS and 100% Nr, and gear retraction while accelerating to BROC speed.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-14 Cat A Horizontal Landing Profile (p.4-24)

items.question: What minimum height above the surface does Figure 4-14 show during a Category A horizontal balked landing?
items.explanation: Figure 4-14 marks a 35 ft minimum during the acceleration to 70 KIAS in the balked landing.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-14 Cat A Horizontal Landing Profile (p.4-24)

items.question: The Category A horizontal landing distance in Figure 4-15 is measured over what segment?
options: From the LDP at 200 ft to a stop
From 50 ft height to a stop
From 50 ft height to a hover
items.explanation: Figure 4-15 is titled horizontal profile landing distance from 50 ft height to stop, one engine inoperative, Vappr 50 KIAS, 600 fpm.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-15 Cat A Horizontal Landing Distance (p.4-25)

items.question: With a crosswind component greater than 20 knots, what must be added to the Figure 4-15 Category A horizontal landing distance?
items.explanation: A note on Figure 4-15 says to add 650 ft to the chart distance when the crosswind component exceeds 20 knots.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-15 Cat A Horizontal Landing Distance (p.4-25)

items.question: In the Category A ground level helipad vertical takeoff profile (Figure 4-16), at what rate is the vertical climb to TDP made?
items.explanation: Figure 4-16 shows a vertical climb to the TDP at 850 to 1150 fpm.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-16 Cat A Vertical Takeoff Profile (p.4-26)

items.question: In the OEI continued takeoff of Figure 4-16 (ground level helipad), what happens after the aircraft reaches Vtoss?
options: The aircraft levels off at 35 ft
items.explanation: In Figure 4-16 the OEI continued takeoff reaches Vtoss first; 2 minute OEI power is selected after that, on the climb-out.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-16 Cat A Vertical Takeoff Profile (p.4-26)

items.question: What is the maximum gross weight on the Category A ground level helipad TDP/Vtoss chart (Figure 4-18)?
items.explanation: Figure 4-18 marks a maximum gross weight of 24,500 lb for Category A ground level helipad operations, below the 26,500 lb aircraft maximum.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-18 Cat A Vertical TDP, Vtoss and Takeoff Distance (p.4-33)

items.question: Per the night operations note on Figure 4-18, what is the maximum TDP for night Category A ground level helipad operations?
options: The lower of 110 ft and the chart maximum reject TDP
The higher of 110 ft and the minimum fly-away TDP
110 ft plus the height of any obstacle
The chart maximum reject TDP, with no fixed cap
items.explanation: The Figure 4-18 note says the maximum TDP for night operations is the minimum of 110 ft or the chart maximum reject TDP; a weight reduction may be needed so the minimum fly-away TDP is 110 ft or less.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-18 Night Operations Note (p.4-33)

items.question: At night, if the minimum fly-away TDP from Figure 4-18 is above 110 ft, what does the chart note require?
options: Use the maximum reject TDP instead
Reduce gross weight until it is 110 ft or less
Add 10 ft to the maximum reject TDP
items.explanation: The night operations note says a reduction in gross weight may be required so that the minimum fly-away TDP is less than or equal to 110 ft.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-18 Night Operations Note (p.4-33)

items.question: What is the minimum TDP marked on the Category A ground level helipad chart (Figure 4-18)?
items.explanation: Figure 4-18 shades a 'MINIMUM TDP ~ 30 FT' band on the minimum fly-away TDP scale.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-18 Cat A Vertical TDP, Vtoss and Takeoff Distance (p.4-33)

items.question: What minimum field length is marked on the Category A ground level helipad takeoff distance scale (Figure 4-18)?
items.explanation: Figure 4-18 marks a 'MINIMUM FIELD LENGTH ~ 600 FT' on the takeoff distance scale.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-18 Cat A Vertical TDP, Vtoss and Takeoff Distance (p.4-33)

items.question: On Figure 4-18, what does the unfactored headwind correction apply to?
items.explanation: The headwind lines on Figure 4-18 are labelled 'unfactored headwind ~ kts (applicable to takeoff distance only)'.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-18 Cat A Vertical TDP, Vtoss and Takeoff Distance (p.4-33)

items.question: In the Figure 4-18 example with a 20 knot direct headwind, which wind line is used to read the takeoff distance?
items.explanation: The example uses the 10 knot wind line, 50% of the 20 knot headwind, consistent with the rule of crediting no more than 50% of the headwind.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-18 determination examples (p.4-30)

items.question: Per the note to the Figure 4-18 examples, what may be done when chart limitations make the maximum reject TDP up to 10 ft lower than the minimum fly-away TDP?
options: Reduce weight until both TDPs are equal
Use the maximum reject TDP and add 10 ft
Use the Figure 4-17 maximum weight and the minimum fly-away TDP
Discard the takeoff at that weight
items.explanation: The note says that in this case it is permissible to use the Figure 4-17 maximum takeoff weight and the minimum fly-away TDP.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-18 determination examples, NOTE (p.4-30)

items.question: In the Figure 4-19 example, a 50 ft obstacle 75 ft from the nose wheel lies outside the exempt region and the no-obstacle minimum fly-away TDP is 85 ft. What is the minimum fly-away TDP?
items.explanation: Because the obstacle point lies above the minimum fly-away TDP, the obstacle height is added: 85 ft + 50 ft = 135 ft.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-19 examples (p.4-37)

items.question: In Figure 4-17 example 1 (sea level, 20°C, no obstacles), the chart reads 25,000 lb. What maximum takeoff weight applies?
items.explanation: Since the maximum allowable gross weight is 24,500 lb, 24,500 lb is also the maximum takeoff weight even though the chart line reads 25,000 lb.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-17 examples (p.4-27)

items.question: In the Category A ground level helipad approach (Figure 4-20), how is the approach flown to the flare?
options: Descend at 600 fpm and 50 KIAS until the flare at 50 ft
Descend at 500 fpm and 35 KIAS until the flare at 50 ft
Descend at 500 fpm and 50 KIAS until the LDP
Descend at 300 fpm and 40 KIAS until 20 ft
items.explanation: Figure 4-20 shows a descent at 500 fpm and 35 KIAS, maintaining 35 KIAS until the flare is initiated at 50 ft.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-20 Cat A Vertical Landing Profile (p.4-39)

items.question: In the Category A ground level helipad balked landing (Figure 4-20), to what speed does the aircraft first accelerate?
items.explanation: Figure 4-20 shows acceleration to Vblss (55 KIAS), selecting 2 minute OEI power, then climbing and accelerating to Vbroc.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-20 Cat A Vertical Landing Profile (p.4-39)

items.question: What approach angle results from a Category A ground level helipad approach flown at 35 KIAS with a 500 fpm descent?
items.explanation: Section IV states that at 35 KIAS and 500 FPM the approach angle is approximately 8.1°.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: CATEGORY A VERTICAL GROUND LEVEL HELIPAD (p.4-2)

items.question: How does a headwind affect the Category A ground level helipad approach angle?
options: It has no effect on the angle
It only affects the LDP height
items.explanation: A headwind increases the approach angle; a faster approach speed or a slower descent rate decreases it.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: CATEGORY A VERTICAL GROUND LEVEL HELIPAD (p.4-2)

items.question: The 'minimum height at balked landing distance' in Figure 4-22 is defined with the aircraft in which climb?
items.explanation: Section IV defines it as the minimum height above the helipad level when the aircraft is in a 55 KIAS climb with 2 minute power selected.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: CATEGORY A VERTICAL GROUND LEVEL HELIPAD (p.4-2)

items.question: Per the note on Figure 4-22, what happens with an LDP of 250 ft?
options: The aircraft can clear a 10 ft obstacle
The balked landing distance becomes zero
The aircraft attains a climbing posture as it passes over the helipad
The approach speed must be raised to 50 KIAS
items.explanation: The Figure 4-22 note says that for an LDP of 250 ft the aircraft attains a climbing posture as it passes over the helipad; the other note concerns the 125 ft minimum LDP clearing a 10 ft obstacle.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-22 Cat A Ground Level Helipad LDP and Balked Landing Distance (p.4-44)

items.question: In Figure 4-22 example 2, what LDP is read for a 50 ft obstacle in the balked landing path?
items.explanation: Entering Figure 4-22 at a 50 ft obstacle gives a minimum height at balked landing distance of 85 ft, a balked landing distance of 665 ft and an LDP of 165 ft.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-22 examples (p.4-43)

items.question: In the Category B takeoff profile (Figure 4-23), at what speed does the aircraft rotate?
items.explanation: Figure 4-23: accelerate using hover torque plus up to 10% at 10 ft wheel height, rotate at 45 KIAS and accelerate to climb at Vy.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-23 Cat B Takeoff Profile (p.4-45)

items.question: In the Category B takeoff profile (Figure 4-23), what power is used for the initial acceleration?
options: Hover torque plus up to 10%, holding 10 ft wheel height
items.explanation: Figure 4-23 shows the acceleration made using hover Q plus up to 10% Q while maintaining 10 ft wheel height; the later climb is at Vy with takeoff power.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-23 Cat B Takeoff Profile (p.4-45)

items.question: To what height is the Category B takeoff distance measured in Figure 4-23?
items.explanation: In Figure 4-23 the takeoff distance ends at 50 ft; the takeoff flight path then continues to 1000 ft.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-23 Cat B Takeoff Profile (p.4-45)

items.question: What correction does Figure 4-24 require for the Category B takeoff distance with anti-ice on?
items.explanation: The Figure 4-24 note says to add 320 ft to the Category B takeoff distance with anti-ice on.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-24 Cat B Takeoff Distance (p.4-46)

items.question: In the Figure 4-24 Category B takeoff distance tables, what do the asterisked values indicate?
options: Data above 11,000 ft DA or the high ambient temperature limit, for interpolation only
Values that include the anti-ice correction
Values valid only with the air conditioner off
Values that need 50% headwind credit applied
items.explanation: The note marks with an asterisk data presented for interpolation only: above 11,000 ft density altitude or the high ambient temperature limit.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-24 Cat B Takeoff Distance (p.4-46)

items.question: How is the Category B landing flown in Figure 4-26?
options: 500 fpm at 35 KIAS, flare at 50 ft
600 fpm at 50 KIAS through 200 ft AGL, flare at 50 ft and 50 KIAS
600 fpm at 70 KIAS, flare at 100 ft
500 fpm at 50 KIAS, flare at 20 ft
items.explanation: Figure 4-26 shows a descent at 600 fpm at 50 KIAS through 200 ft AGL and a deceleration flare initiated at 50 KIAS at 50 ft.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-26 Cat B Landing Profile (p.4-50)

items.question: How does the end point of the Category B landing distance (Figure 4-27) differ from the Category A horizontal landing distance (Figure 4-15)?
options: Category B is measured to a stop; Category A to a hover
Category B is measured to a hover; Category A to a stop
Category B is measured from 200 ft; Category A from 50 ft
items.explanation: Figure 4-27 gives landing distance from 50 ft height to hover; Figure 4-15 gives landing distance from 50 ft height to stop.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-27 Cat B Landing Distance (p.4-51); Figure 4-15 (p.4-25)

items.question: Figure 4-25 (all engines forward climb) is drawn for which conditions?
options: Takeoff power, Vy, 100% Nr, gear down
Maximum continuous power, Vtoss, 100% Nr, gear up
30 minute power, BROC speed, 105% Nr, gear down
Maximum continuous power, BROC speed, 105% Nr, gear up
items.explanation: Figure 4-25 is headed dual engine, maximum continuous power, best rate of climb speed, 105% Nr, gear up, below 14,000 ft HP.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-25 AEO Forward Climb Performance (p.4-48)

items.question: In the Figure 4-25 AEO climb at 26,500 lb, what rate-of-climb reduction applies for RIPS and anti-ice on above 4,000 ft?
items.explanation: The Figure 4-25 table gives 1,300 fpm for RIPS and anti-ice on above 4,000 ft at 26,500 lb, against 600 fpm at or below 4,000 ft.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-25 AEO Forward Climb Performance (p.4-48)

items.question: On the Hover OGE takeoff power chart (Figure 4-28), how much must maximum gross weight be reduced for a crosswind or tailwind at 20°C?
items.explanation: For other than calm wind with the relative wind outside the sector ahead of the nose, the Figure 4-28 table gives a 600 lb reduction for crosswind or tailwind at 20°C.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-28 Hover OGE, Takeoff Power (p.4-52)

items.question: On the Hover OGE takeoff power chart (Figure 4-28), how much must maximum gross weight be reduced with anti-ice on at 0°C?
items.explanation: The Figure 4-28 table gives a 1,400 lb reduction for anti-ice on at 0°C (575 lb for crosswind/tailwind, 375 lb for the air conditioner).
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-28 Hover OGE, Takeoff Power (p.4-52)

items.question: What is the highest point of the avoid area on the S-92 height-velocity diagram (Figure 4-31) at zero airspeed?
items.explanation: The shaded avoid area of Figure 4-31 reaches 400 ft indicated altitude at 0 knots and extends out to about 40 knots.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-31 Height-Velocity Diagram (p.4-56)

items.question: Which test conditions apply to the S-92 height-velocity diagram (Figure 4-31)?
options: Hard surface, winds 5 kt or less, straight path, gear down at entry
Any surface, winds up to 20 kt, gear up at entry
Hard surface, calm wind, gear up, 100% Nr
Helideck, winds 10 kt or less, gear down at entry
items.explanation: Figure 4-31 lists hard surface runway, winds 5 kts or less, straight takeoff and climbout path, and gear down at entry; it applies at the maximum allowable Category B takeoff gross weight.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-31 Height-Velocity Diagram (p.4-56)

items.question: The OEI hover OGE capability chart with 30 second power (Figure 4-32) is drawn at which torque limit?
items.explanation: Figure 4-32 is headed OEI 30 second power, 100% Nr, 141% Q-limit; the 2 minute chart (Figure 4-34) shows a 120% OEI transmission torque limit.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-32 OEI HOGE Capability 30 Sec Power (p.4-57)

items.question: Which torque limit is marked on the OEI hover OGE capability chart for 2 minute power (Figure 4-34)?
items.explanation: Figure 4-34 (OEI 2 minute power, 100% Nr) marks the 120% OEI transmission torque limit.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: Figure 4-34 OEI HOGE Capability 2 Min Power (p.4-59)

items.question: Which S-92A certified noise level is highest?
items.explanation: The certified levels are 94.5 EPNdB takeoff, 97.5 approach and 97.2 flyover; the flyover level is based on a VH of 150.5 KTAS.
references: S-92 RFM Part 1 Sec IV: NOISE LEVEL CERTIFICATION (p.4-61)
